minor.issue: No way to un-set (delete) a rotated secret from the UI/API — once configured, a workspace is locked into signature verification. Consider POST /api/pos/rotate-secret with {provider, clear:true} or DELETE /api/pos/secret/{provider} for dev/rollback.

Uses random.choices (not secrets.SystemRandom) for the whsec_ payload — cryptographically-secret secrets should come from secrets.token_urlsafe(30) or secrets.SystemRandom to avoid predictable Mersenne-Twister output. Same concern applies to _api_key_str().
PDF renderer includes stats.impressions in the coupons table but there's no equivalent 'impressions' column in the CSV — small parity gap; boards will see a KPI in the PDF that's missing in the CSV.

period=999 silently falls back to 30 without any hint to the caller. Consider echoing the applied period in a response header (e.g. X-PromoOS-Period-Applied: 30) or returning 400 for out-of-range periods.

Unknown variant silently falls back to inline — technically per spec, but there's no telemetry, log, or 400 to surface merchant typos ('populp' instead of 'popup'). Consider a debug header X-PromoOS-Variant-Applied when variant differs from requested.

CAC formula uses total_discount/new_n but new_n falls back to 1 when there are 0 new-segment customers, which silently inflates CAC to = total_discount (looks like $61 CAC even when there are zero acquired customers). Recommend returning null/0 when new_n==0 rather than dividing by 1.

issues: Chart parent div uses minHeight:320 but Recharts still logs 2 startup warnings 'The width(-1) and height(-1) of chart should be greater than 0' (same regression as iter-4/5). Also the AreaChart renders a single flat line because /analytics/timeseries returns 0-revenue days for this workspace — user-facing but caused by seed data, not the chart.
Woocommerce is spelled 'Woocommerce' (single-word) — canonical brand is 'WooCommerce' (camelcase). Cosmetic.

React hydration warning: '<option> cannot be a child of <span>'. Root cause: Emergent instrumentation injects <span> nodes inside every child of <select>; the raw <option> markup in Analytics.js line 66 is fine — this is dev-toolchain noise, safe to ignore in prod, but the warning is visible on every /analytics load.

action_items: OPTIONAL: Add DELETE / clear-secret endpoint for POS webhooks so merchants can revert to trust-mode during dev without dropping the workspace doc.
OPTIONAL: Swap random.choices → secrets.token_urlsafe(30) in rotate_pos_secret() and _api_key_str() for cryptographically-strong tokens.
OPTIONAL: Return metrics.cac as 0.0 (or null) when there are no new customers, instead of dividing total_discount by fallback new_n=1 (currently inflates CAC).
OPTIONAL: Emit X-PromoOS-Variant-Applied response header on /embed/coupon.js so merchants notice typo'd variant params.
OPTIONAL: Impressions column parity between CSV and PDF exports.
OPTIONAL (carried over from iter-5): Split /app/backend/server.py (now 2441 lines) into routers/{auth,coupons,pos,journeys,ai,analytics,exports,embed,customers}.py.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py grew from 2100 → 2441 lines. HMAC + exports + variants added ~340 LOC in one file. Router split is now overdue.

_hmac_ok uses hmac.compare_digest correctly (constant-time), but the secret is stored PLAINTEXT in db.workspaces.webhook_secrets.shopify — an attacker with read access to Mongo can forge signatures. Consider hashing the secret at rest and comparing base64(hmac-sha256(plaintext, raw)) via a KDF-derived key, OR encrypting the secret with an app-wide KMS key.
_get_workspace_secret is defined but never used — shopify_webhook and woocommerce_webhook read the secret inline from ws.get('webhook_secrets'). Dead code; either use it or remove it.

The whsec_ generation uses random.choices(ascii_letters+digits, k=40) which is Mersenne-Twister-seeded — sufficient for identifier uniqueness but NOT for cryptographic secrets. Migrate to secrets.token_urlsafe(30).

/analytics/export builds the PDF in-memory via reportlab.SimpleDocTemplate — for workspaces with thousands of coupons the .to_list(500) cap on coupons + hard 20 top-coupon cap prevents runaway, but no pagination for the underlying redemption fetch (20000-doc cap). If a heavy workspace exceeds 20k redemptions in a 365-day window the report silently truncates. Add a `truncated: true` warning to the CSV/PDF footer.
period fallback logic ('if period not in (7,14,...): period=30') silently ignores the caller's intent. Prefer HTTPException(400) + suggested list, or an X-Applied-Period response header.
The embed renderers duplicate ~40 lines of style boilerplate across all 5 variants. Extract a shared _CSS_HEADER constant + _brand_style(d) helper to make future variant additions safer.

_apply_from_pos writes redemption docs with source='shopify'|'woocommerce' but the HMAC verification lives in the webhook handler — an attacker who bypasses signature check (e.g. via the same code path as _apply_from_pos being reused elsewhere) can still write source='shopify' redemptions. Consider moving _apply_from_pos into an internal helper that takes a `verified: bool` flag and refuses to write when False.

IMPORTANT: because the tests rotate webhook_secrets many times, after this suite runs the workspace has webhook_secrets.{shopify,woocommerce} set to the LAST test run's secret. If a downstream test expects unsigned webhooks to work in trust mode, either (a) manually remove `webhook_secrets` from db.workspaces, or (b) fetch the latest secret via /pos/rotate-secret first and sign accordingly. HMAC signing pattern in tests: use `requests.post(..., data=raw_body_bytes, headers={..., 'X-Shopify-Hmac-Sha256': base64(hmac.new(secret, raw, sha256).digest())})` — do NOT pass json= or the body bytes will differ from the signed bytes.
